t: This is the site of the Great Synagogue of London, which is no longer standing. For centuries it was the centre of Ashkenazi Jewish life in London, an Orthodox congregation just north of Aldgate in the City. It was built in the seventeenth century and destroyed in the Blitz during the Second World War. The building you'd have seen was designed by James Spiller, an architect and surveyor who was a close associate of Sir John Soane. Spiller also designed the church of St John-at-Hackney.
